rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 2-3 - authors fabricated the applicator and tested it at CCSHAU Hisar, recording dripper/sprinkler discharge, insolation and panel/battery voltage. Q2: Abstract, Section 3.2 and Conclusions - the machine with drip was evaluated in a bottle gourd crop and its performance was reported as satisfactory for saving the crop under dry spell conditions; Table 2 gives dripper discharge 79.9 ml/min and Table 3 insolation 948 W/m2.
rows.notes: The crop-rescue result is only a qualitative statement; no crop survival, yield, soil moisture or stress measurements are reported, so the evidence on the claimed effect is very thin. Discharge and insolation data come from a commercial test report (ref 10) by the testing centre where one author works. Only one site, one crop, one short test period. Q4: emitter discharge is a machine hydraulic parameter, not soil or plant water status. Q7: statements that water must come from a rainwater pond and that bunding/deep ploughing help are design/recommendations, not findings. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: Tables 2-3 give SDs for discharge rate and insolation, but no dispersion for the crop-rescue effect itself; test year is inconsistent (2018 vs 2019).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 2-3 - own machine fabrication and test data on discharge, insolation and voltage.
rows.notes: The study reports no measurement of water use, water-use efficiency or water saving. The only efficiency figures (85% application efficiency for drip, 30-70% water saving) are generic assertions or cited from other work (refs 3, 5), not results of this study. Own results are limited to emitter discharge rates, solar insolation, voltages and a qualitative statement that bottle gourd was saved under dry spell.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3 and 3.2, Tables 2-3 - own machine fabrication and test data.
rows.notes: No yield, biomass or production data are reported for any crop. The study only states qualitatively that the machine's performance in bottle gourd was satisfactory to save the crop under dry spell conditions; claims about increased yield and sustainable production in the Introduction/Conclusions are assertions or cited from other work. Not treated as own evidence on crop production.

notes: Short machine-development note. Own data consist of ten discharge-rate tests, a one-day insolation/voltage series (sourced from a commercial test report by the authors' testing centre) and an unquantified statement that the machine saved a bottle gourd crop under dry spell. No agronomic, water-use or economic measurements. Test date inconsistent (January 2018 in Section 3.2 vs January 2019 in Abstract).
